findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default target environment used by `bridge status` when no explicit target option is supplied (e.g. default to the local writer id `local:<repo-env-id>`), so the FOREIGN vs HEALTHY verdict is deterministic.
evidence: Plan states the last-pass WRITER id defaults to `local:<repo-env-id>` when unset
Plan: 'Status accepts an explicit target environment option, and the canary explicitly requests reconciler' — but does not state the status READER's default target when the option is omitted
FOREIGN is defined as 'durable record environment differs from the explicitly selected target', which presupposes a selected target
findings.finding: The default target environment for a plain `bridge status` invocation (no explicit target option) is not stated, leaving the FOREIGN vs HEALTHY verdict ambiguous for a developer's local last-pass record.
findings.location: Environment identity + Status snapshot: `bridge status` verdict FOREIGN
scenarios: A developer runs `bridge status` with no --target after a local reconciler pass; unclear whether the local record reads HEALTHY (default target = local:<repo-env-id>) or FOREIGN (default target = reconciler)
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that an omitted status target defaults to the same identity rule as the writer (`local:<repo-env-id>` outside CI), so a local record reads HEALTHY locally and only becomes FOREIGN when a caller explicitly targets `reconciler`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the last-pass ref CAS write reuses the existing shared seams (`_push_lease_cas` for the force-with-lease push, `_cas_once`/`_is_cas_mismatch_stderr` for mismatch classification, and the `_cas_advance_with_retry` backoff-loop pattern) rather than open-coding a parallel git-push + retry + stderr classifier.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:748 `_push_lease_cas` already does `git push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<old>` and translates rejection into the shared exit-128 CAS shape
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_advisory_lock.py:294 `_cas_once` is the documented single-shot CAS seam; _ref_lock builds acquire/release/steal/renew on it

docs/adr/0031-reconciler-ref-lock.md:713 comment 'keeping exactly one CAS discriminator' and ADR note that `_cas_advance_with_retry becomes _cas_once in a retry loop` — a reusable backoff-loop pattern prior tickets already reused (operator_attested_ac_corpus references reusing `_cas_advance_with_retry`/`_is_cas_mismatch`)

The plan names a new ref refs/reconciler/last-pass and a bespoke 100ms/200ms 3-attempt loop without stating whether it routes through _push_lease_cas / _cas_once or open-codes a parallel implementation
findings.finding: The last-pass ref writer specifies its own --force-with-lease CAS push, three-attempt retry, and mismatch/refetch backoff, which overlaps the existing shared CAS infrastructure in _ref_lock.py/_advisory_lock.py; the plan does not state it reuses those seams, risking an NIH second CAS-mismatch classifier.
findings.location: Plan section 'Durable state and writer contract' — 'Update the ref with observed-OID compare-and-swap using --force-with-lease=... Make at most three total attempts, refetching after each CAS mismatch and sleeping 100 ms then 200 ms'
scenarios: A developer implements a fresh git-push + stderr classification for the last-pass ref, producing a second CAS-mismatch discriminator that diverges from _is_cas_mismatch_stderr's fail-closed marker logic
The bespoke 3-attempt loop duplicates _cas_advance_with_retry's refetch-and-backoff logic instead of reusing it
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the writer contract: the last-pass ref advance goes through the existing `_ref_lock`/`_advisory_lock` CAS seam (`_push_lease_cas` + `_cas_once`), parameterizing the retry count (3) and backoff (100ms/200ms) on the shared retry helper, so no second CAS-mismatch discriminator is introduced.

findings.checklist_item: Add an acceptance criterion that the defaulted `bridge status` heartbeat path is exercised end-to-end/live by the canary — real reconciler ref fetch plus two-snapshot fence classification (RUNNING and CRASHED) against actual refs, not a mocked/fixtured status substitute.
evidence: 'Production defaults the canary heartbeat source to canonical bridge status.'
'takes two snapshots when a lock is present' and 'unchanged OID/fence as CRASHED'
Verification bullet asserts canary 'consumes canonical status' but does not state the two-snapshot read runs against real reconciler refs end-to-end vs a stubbed status/ref substitute.
findings.finding: This is a cutover that makes canonical `bridge status` the DEFAULT canary heartbeat source, but the verification plan does not explicitly commit the defaulted path (canary taking two live snapshots against real `refs/reconciler/*`) to a live/end-to-end exercise rather than fixture/mocked ref reads; the highest-risk defaulted behavior (two-snapshot CRASHED classification across the observed lease) could pass green offline while the live git-ref read path is broken.
findings.location: Verification plan bullet: 'canary fetches reconciler refs, consumes canonical status, preserves ticket escalation, defaults away from heartbeat API queries' and Canary cutover section
scenarios: A canary test that mocks the status output or fixtures the ref reads goes green while the real `+refs/reconciler/*:refs/reconciler/*` fetch + two-snapshot fence comparison is broken in production, letting the cutover close without ever running the defaulted live path.
RUNNING-vs-CRASHED classification passes on fake fences but misfires on real lock-blob lease metadata in CI.
findings.suggested_fix: State that at least one held-out canary E2E test drives the real two-snapshot flow against live `refs/reconciler/*` (RUNNING advancing fence and CRASHED stalled fence), and that the offline github-api rollback test is additive rather than the sole coverage of the defaulted path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify exactly which fence value the last-pass record captures (e.g. the final heartbeat fence at finalization) and how `bridge status` correlates that recorded fence with the live lock fence when distinguishing RUNNING from a completed pass.
evidence: Plan: 'the lock fence observed for the pass' and 'RUNNING, lock currently held ... include lock OID, fence, and lease.'
_ref_lock.py renew() bumps fence each heartbeat (fence+1); __main__.py finally stops heartbeat then releases against the latest renewed oid — the fence is a moving value across the pass
ABSENCE: plan does not define which fence snapshot is authoritative in the record
findings.finding: The writer contract says the record contains 'the lock fence observed for the pass', but the fence is advanced continuously by the daemon heartbeat during the pass and is stopped in the finally block before release; the plan does not specify WHICH fence value is captured (acquisition fence vs. last heartbeat fence) nor how status correlates that recorded fence against the live lock OID/fence when reporting RUNNING.
findings.location: Durable state and writer contract; Status snapshot and exact contract (RUNNING clause)
scenarios: A pass runs long enough for several heartbeat fence bumps; the recorded fence is ambiguous and may not correspond to any single lock state a status reader can correlate.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the deploy ordering / coexistence so the reconciler last-pass writer is live and has written `refs/reconciler/last-pass` before the canary default flips to `status`, or document the github-api rollback as the coexistence path during the window.
evidence: Plan: 'Production defaults the canary heartbeat source to canonical bridge status'
Plan: NEVER_RUN, no durable last-pass record and no live lock, exit 1
Absence: no statement of whether the reconciler last-pass writer must ship (and run at least once) before the canary default flips to status, nor old+new coexistence during the window
findings.finding: Deploy ordering between the ref-producing reconciler and the canary cutover is not specified; if the canary defaults to `status` before the reconciler has written any `refs/reconciler/last-pass`, status reports NEVER_RUN (exit 1) as a false alarm during rollout.
scenarios: Canary defaults to status in production before the reconciler has performed a finalization that writes the ref — canary sees NEVER_RUN and escalates a false failure
findings.suggested_fix: Add a rollout ordering note: keep `REBAR_CANARY_HEARTBEAT_SOURCE=github-api` until at least one reconciler pass has advanced `refs/reconciler/last-pass`, then flip the default to `status`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the invariant that the lock-held, fence-non-advancing finalization window (CAS retries + release) is bounded far below one lease, so the canary's lease-separated snapshots can never observe a finalizing pass as CRASHED.
evidence: Plan: 'While CAS retries, the lock remains held and status reports RUNNING.' and 'unchanged OID/fence as CRASHED'
__main__.py finally: heartbeat.stop() precedes release — no fence advance during finalization
_ref_lock.DEFAULT_LEASE_SECS=120 >> ~300ms retry window, so the race is not real but is unstated
findings.finding: The plan states finalization keeps the lock held while last-pass CAS retries (up to 300ms backoff plus push latency), but the existing finalization stops the heartbeat before release, so the lock fence does not advance during that window; the plan does not state that this non-advancing window is bounded well below one lease so a concurrent canary snapshot pair cannot misread finalizing-RUNNING as CRASHED.
findings.location: Durable state and writer contract; Status snapshot and exact contract (CRASHED clause)
scenarios: Canary happens to take its two snapshots straddling a finalization window.
